data.content: Plan 2 days in Anuradhapura for ancient history, for two French adults starting from Colombo. We already have a hotel.

Wikivoyage guide for Anuradhapura (all topics):
[Introduction] Anuradhapura is a UNESCO World Heritage listed city in the North Central Province of Sri Lanka.
[Understand] As an ancient capital of Sri Lanka and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Anuradhapura is worth visiting for its well-preserved ruins that show off early Sri Lankan civilization. Established in the 4th centure BCE, the city served as a centre for Buddhist scholarship and monastic life for over 1000 years, drawing flocks of monks and pilgrims. Pilgrims still flock to various sites on holy days today. ...
[Get in] By plane: As of 2025 there are no scheduled flights to the airport. Air Senok or Helitours may operate charter flights. 1 Anuradhapura Airport (ACJ IATA), Airport Rd. (updated May 2015) By bus: From Colombo, slower non-AC buses go from Central Bus Station (Find routes 4, 15, 57; Rs. 350) and slightly quicker AC/Luxury/Private buses go from the nearby Bastian Mawatha Bus Station, terminal 3 (5 hrs, every half hour, until 18:30). ...
[Get around] Tuk tuks and buses are abundant. The PickMe app is the ridesharing app of choice here, for motorbikes, tuk tuks and taxis. The New Town is relatively small, and can be walked from one end to another in half an hour. This old town is quite large, so get a tuk-tuk if you want to cover all the sights in one day (should be Rs 3,500-4,500 per tour in 2023). ...
[See] The ancient city of Anuradhapura was first settled ca. 900 BCE, and served off and on as the capital of the Sinhalese Kingdom until ca. 1100 CE, when the capital moved further south. The city was quite large in its heyday, and so there is a lot of archaeology to see. 1 Bodhi Tree Temple (The Sri Maha Bodhiya). ...
[Do] Apart from seeing the archaeology of the ancient city, it is possible to explore the area, and to spend time in the Anuradhapura New Town. There are many shops in the New Town, as well as a market, and the interested visitor may wish to patronize some of these. There are guided city tours offered by bicycle or on foot through local tour agencies, or ask at your hotel. You can also swim in the Tissa Wewa with the locals. ...
[Sleep] There are numerous guest houses Anuradhapura new town, and many more budget accommodations. Prices at hostels start from Rs 1,500 to 2,000 per person for a night. If you don't have and idea of where you'll be staying, any tuk-tuk driver will be happy to offer you rooms that he or his brother is renting, usually offering very basic comfort at a reasonable, negotiable price. ...
[Stay safe] Beware of the monkeys. Monkeys, particularly macaques (small, red-faced monkeys) can get quite aggressive, and have been known to steal unattended personal belongs.
[Stay healthy] Sri Lanka was declared a malaria-free zone by the WHO in 2016 but, there remains a risk of dengue fever locally. Venomous snakes inhabit this area. Do not walk through long grass, and don't stick your hands into holes in masonry or stone structures.
Sections ending in ... were shortened; full article: https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Anuradhapura

Wikivoyage guide for Anuradhapura (see and do):
[See] The ancient city of Anuradhapura was first settled ca. 900 BCE, and served off and on as the capital of the Sinhalese Kingdom until ca. 1100 CE, when the capital moved further south. The city was quite large in its heyday, and so there is a lot of archaeology to see. 1 Bodhi Tree Temple (The Sri Maha Bodhiya). The second most sacred place in Sri Lanka, after the Sri Dalada Maligawa (Temple of the Tooth) in Kandy and also part of the eight sacred places in Sri Lanka. The Bodhi Tree is allegedly a cutting from the original Bodhi tree under which the Buddha gained enlightenment, and has been continuously guarded for over 2,000 years, making it the oldest historically authenticated tree in the world. The temple complex is surrounded by walls, and is quite busy with monks and worshipers. Due to terrorist activities in the 1980s, it is not possible to drive up to the temple, and one must go through a metal detector before entering the complex. Bags will be checked. Shoes can be left near the entrance. It is polite to leave a tip. Free. (updated Jan 2018) 2 Ruwanwelisaya. ...
[Do] Apart from seeing the archaeology of the ancient city, it is possible to explore the area, and to spend time in the Anuradhapura New Town. There are many shops in the New Town, as well as a market, and the interested visitor may wish to patronize some of these. There are guided city tours offered by bicycle or on foot through local tour agencies, or ask at your hotel. You can also swim in the Tissa Wewa with the locals. There are also swimming spots in the river near the Jetavanarama Dagoba.

# 2-day trip to Anuradhapura

A 2-day historical itinerary from Colombo to Anuradhapura tailored for two French adults. Explore ancient UNESCO World Heritage stupas, sacred temples, and historical reservoirs, concluding with an excursion to nearby Mihintale.

**Starting point:** Colombo

## Day 1: Arrival from Colombo & Sacred Sites
*Weather:* 2026-11-23: moderate rain showers; min 24.3 °C, max 29.9 °C; chance of precipitation 93%; rainfall 8.0 mm; max wind 12.3 km/h (Open-Meteo)
*Travel:* Colombo to Anuradhapura: 209 km, about 3 h 44 min by car without traffic (OSRM)
- **Afternoon: Bodhi Tree Temple (The Sri Maha Bodhiya)** (about 2 h) - Visit the venerated Bodhi Tree Temple, housing the oldest historically authenticated tree in the world, continuously guarded for over 2,000 years. _(Wikivoyage)_
- **Evening: Tissa Wewa** (about 1.5 h) - Relax along the banks of this ancient artificial reservoir, enjoying scenic views and local surroundings. _(Wikivoyage)_

## Day 2: Ancient Monuments & Mihintale Excursion
*Weather:* 2026-11-24: thunderstorm; min 23.8 °C, max 29.1 °C; chance of precipitation 100%; rainfall 14.5 mm; max wind 12.5 km/h (Open-Meteo)
*Travel:* Anuradhapura to Mihintale: 16 km, about 21 min by car without traffic (OSRM)
- **Morning: Ruwanwelisaya** (about 2 h) - Explore the magnificent white stupa built by King Dutugemunu, an iconic architectural marvel of ancient Sri Lanka. _(Wikivoyage)_
- **Afternoon: Jetavanarama Dagoba** (about 2 h) - Marvel at one of the largest brick structures of the ancient world, surrounded by archaeological ruins. _(Wikivoyage)_
- **Evening: Mihintale** (about 2.5 h) - Take a short drive to Mihintale, the sacred mountain site regarded as the cradle of Buddhism in Sri Lanka. _(Wikivoyage)_

## Other costs (estimates from Wikivoyage, may be out of date)
- **Tuk-tuk tour of the ancient city**
  - Price: LKR 4,500 (USD 13.54) (shared) x 1
  - Quantity: 1 tuk-tuk tour for the group, as quoted in Wikivoyage guide (Rs 3,500-4,500 per tour)
  - Per person: LKR 2,250 (USD 6.77)
  - For the group: LKR 4,500 (USD 13.54)

## Trip budget
- Group: 2 non-SAARC foreign adults
- Verified entrance fees: LKR 0 (USD 0)
- Other estimated costs: LKR 4,500 (USD 13.54)
- TOTAL estimated budget for the group: LKR 4,500 (USD 13.54)
- Per person: LKR 2,250 (USD 6.77)
- **Not included (no reliable source here)**
  - Accommodation (you said you have your own)
  - Food and drinks
  - Transport fares (buses, trains, tuk-tuks, a driver)
  - Guides, tips and personal spending
- Other-currency amounts use 1 USD = 332.39 LKR (indicative mid-market rate); a source's own LKR figure is used as given.

## Practical information
- Driving from Colombo to Anuradhapura covers 209 km and takes approximately 3 hours 44 minutes by car in free-flow traffic. _(OSRM)_
- The ancient city area is expansive, so hiring a tuk-tuk is recommended to cover the main ruins efficiently. _(Wikivoyage)_
- Be cautious with small macaque monkeys near temple sites as they may grab unattended items. _(Wikivoyage)_
- Sri Lanka is malaria-free, but mosquito protection is recommended due to local dengue fever risks. _(Wikivoyage)_
- The Sri Maha Bodhi tree is revered as a cutting from the original tree under which the Buddha attained enlightenment. _(Wikivoyage)_

## Suggestions
_General advice, not checked against live data._
- Please check the current visa (ETA) rules on the official Sri Lanka immigration website before your trip.
- Wear modest clothing covering shoulders and knees when visiting sacred temple grounds, and remove footwear and headwear before entering.
- Keep personal items secure and avoid feeding or approaching macaques around the ancient ruins.
- Use mosquito repellent and wear light clothing to protect against dengue fever.

## Assumptions
- Travel time estimates assume private car driving without traffic or stops.
- The travellers already have hotel accommodation booked in Anuradhapura.

## Please note
- Mihintale: not found in the tool results for Anuradhapura; check it before you go.
